summary:
A³D – 30 SOLS: SURVIVE MARS is an interactive educational Mars survival simulation game developed by Team A³D. Players manage a Mars research outpost for 30 Martian days (Sols), balancing essential resources such as power, oxygen, and food while responding to simulated environmental hazards.

The game also integrates real space-weather notifications from NASA's DONKI API into its mission history. By combining resource management, decision-making, simulated Mars hazards, and real NASA data, A³D helps players understand the challenges of sustaining human life and preparing for future exploration of Mars.
details:
A³D – 30 SOLS: SURVIVE MARS is an interactive survival simulation game that demonstrates the challenges of maintaining a human research outpost on Mars.

The player starts with limited resources: power, oxygen, and food. Each Martian day (Sol) consumes resources, and the player has two actions per Sol to maintain the outpost.

The available actions include:

• Solar Array: Generates power for the outpost.
• Oxygen Unit: Produces oxygen using power.
• Greenhouse: Produces food using power.
• Radiation Shield: Uses power to reduce radiation exposure.

The game introduces simulated radiation events and dust storms, making resource management and decision-making important for survival.

A³D also connects to NASA's DONKI Space Weather Database API to retrieve real space-weather notifications. These notifications, including events such as Radiation Belt Enhancements (RBE) and Coronal Mass Ejections (CME), are recorded in the in-game Mission History.

The objective is to keep the outpost operational and survive 30 Sols.

The project was developed using JavaScript and Phaser 3, with Vite for development and production building. It uses NASA's DONKI API for real space-weather notifications and Netlify for public hosting.

Our goal is to make Mars exploration concepts more accessible through interactive gameplay and demonstrate the importance of resource management and space-weather awareness in future human missions.
